models.qualification: The foundation captions this exact park bronze as installed in 1886, but Carl Jacobsen’s letter of 31 December 1887 reports its arrival and plans for the pedestal. Use the 1880s and leave the exact casting date unknown. A January 1886 letter discusses a proposed de Angelis purchase; it does not by itself establish the final foundry or manufacture country. The largest 1920 px publisher thumbnail and 1500 px foundation photograph were actually inspected. Identical mottled weathering confirms the exact object. The source thumbnail looks pale grey and is tagged black-and-white, while the foundation photo shows green-black bronze patina. Native color/material comparison is REQUIRED before approval. The thumbnail crops the lower legs/base, so completeness there is also pending native views.

Exact Monforte fountain, identified by scanner location and the city’s primary illustrated garden guide, printed page 31 (PDF page 32), plus municipal garden inventory. City source identifies marble and pebble pedestal. Do not transfer the separate Neptune at Glorieta, Jardines de Neptuno, or any ancient prototype metadata. Production country and dimensions are unpublished in pinned evidence. The largest 1920 px thumbnail was actually inspected: mature bearded reclining man, coherent body, marine creature and vegetation-covered plinth. Trident/finger damage is visible. The city’s 13 September 2022 restoration notice documents reattachment of fingers and trident fragments after vandalism; the 2021 scan predates that physical repair. No digital completion authorized. Back/underside and vegetation capture integrity remain pending native review.
